Process_Text.original: All samples were fabricated using an in-house developed 3-axis L-DED system equipped with a 1 kW fibre laser (IPG Photonics Corporation). The wavelength of the laser is 1070 nm, and its nominal beam size is 1 mm. During the fabrication process, the powders were delivered by argon as the carrier and purge gas through a coaxial printing nozzle (COAX14 v5, Fraunhofer USA, Inc.). To ensure accurately controlled powder delivery, a powder feeder (PF 2/2, GTV GmbH) with PLC-control and mass flow meters was used. The laser power, scan speed, and powder feed rate are set to be consistent at 450 W, 4 mm/s, and 0.175 g/min, respectively. The powders are gas atomized spherical with a size distribution of 15–45 μm (EOS GmbH). For homogeneous 316L samples, no powder switching was applied.

Process_Text.original: All samples were fabricated using an in-house developed 3-axis L-DED system equipped with a 1 kW fibre laser (IPG Photonics Corporation). The wavelength of the laser is 1070 nm, and its nominal beam size is 1 mm. During the fabrication process, the powders were delivered by argon as the carrier and purge gas through a coaxial printing nozzle (COAX14 v5, Fraunhofer USA, Inc.). To ensure accurately controlled powder delivery, a powder feeder (PF 2/2, GTV GmbH) with PLC-control and mass flow meters was used. The laser power, scan speed, and powder feed rate are set to be consistent at 450 W, 4 mm/s, and 0.175 g/min, respectively. In the fabrication process, two hoppers storing 316L and PH17-4 powders were alternatively turned on and off, with 15 s pause between each alternation for the powder stream to stabilize. Both the hatch spacing and the number of passes before powder switching were changed to achieve varying lamellae width. For Sample A, the layer thickness is 0.38 mm. The powders are gas atomized spherical with a size distribution of 15–45 μm (EOS GmbH).

Process_Info.Equipment: in-house 3-axis L-DED system, 1 kW fibre laser (IPG Photonics), COAX14 v5 nozzle (Fraunhofer USA), PF 2/2 powder feeder (GTV GmbH)

Microstructure_Text.original: Good bonding with clear boundaries is observed between the 316L regions and the PH17-4 regions. The 316L regions show cellular structures with various morphologies as a result of constitutional supercooling, while in the PH17-4 regions a large number of martensite laths are found. The samples are comprised of mainly two phases, i.e., face centred cubic (FCC) and body centred cubic (BCC), corresponding to 316L and PH17-4, respectively. No defect is found at the boundaries, indicating strong inter-material bonding. The interface between lath martensite and austenite exhibits Kurdjumov-Sachs (K-S) orientation relationship: (111)γ // (101)α’, [011]γ // [111]α’. The interplanar misfit is 2.09%, indicating a coherent interface. No precipitates were identified. All samples show a porosity <0.1% and are thus considered to be fully dense.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Heterostructure composed of distinct 316L (FCC) and PH17-4 (BCC) regions with clear coherent interfaces (K-S orientation, misfit 2.09%). No precipitates. Fully dense with porosity <0.1%.
